outputs.explanation: The scatter plot shows each of the n=141 samples as an individual marker (not an average), and the accompanying histograms are built directly from these raw individual measurements, so the underlying data are fully visible.
Each symbol represents only the mean ± s.d. of 6 (or 3-5) technical/biological replicates per reporter; the individual replicate measurements behind each mean are not plotted anywhere in the panel.

The density curves show fitted normal distributions of subtype-averaged periods/amplitudes, where each curve is derived from only n=1-4 cell-line averages (which are themselves averages of 3-6 replicates). No individual cell-line data points are overlaid on the smooth curves, obscuring the very low number of values underlying each distribution.
The box plots have the individual ridge-length data points (color-coded by reporter) overlaid on top of each box, so the raw values behind the summary statistics are visible.

Each polar histogram bar height reflects the actual distribution of many individual Bmal1-Per2 phase-difference measurements (n = 15-36 combinations per cell line as stated), so the underlying individual data are represented via the histogram itself.

The subtype-level polar histogram pools only n=1-4 cell-line-level (already-averaged) distributions per subtype, and no individual cell-line curves or points are shown within this panel to convey the variability among the few contributing cell lines.

This panel is a schematic/illustrative example of the fitting procedure on a single representative signal, not a summary of averaged data across replicates, so individual data points are not applicable.
Each point represents one of the n=117 individual samples plotted directly (error bars reflect fit parameter uncertainty, not inter-sample averaging), so individual data are already displayed.
